lines.text: PERFORM is where you play the sound.
Its controls are named for what you hear, and nothing in it stops the music.
Two rows of your computer keyboard are keys: A to L for the white notes, W to P for the black.
Z and X move the octave. Hold Shift for an accent.
On the screen, strike a key lower down for a harder note.
A MIDI keyboard plays too, with velocity and pitch bend.
And velocity can play the timbre. With the touch row on Bright, soft notes come out darker and hard ones brighter.
Six controls are named for what they do to the sound: Bright, Snap, Motion, Body, Grit and Space.
Hold a chord and ride Bright up. The sound swells, and the note never breaks.
Underneath, the real knobs move with it.
When a patch loads, PERFORM nudges each of its knobs and listens, then wires every control to the few knobs that move the sound its way.
So Bright means brighter on every patch, however that patch gets there.
Long-press a control to hear what it does here.
Some controls only go one way.
This pad is already as close as it gets, so Space only turns toward far, and the line under it says so.
An amber control with a dashed ring is one this patch can't honestly reach.
Turn it anyway, and it asks for a sound that can.
Grit springs back, and a variant grows in B, labelled with what you asked for.
It isn't aimed at grit yet, so listen before you take it.
The XY pad puts two controls under one hand.
Choose its axes up here.
Then hold a chord, and draw.
The dials follow the dot, so you always see where you are.
Press Offer, and a variant of what you're playing grows in slot B.
It follows your hands. Every note you play sounds in both.
Hold Peek to hear B alone.
Or ride Blend across. B plays at matched loudness, so you judge the sound, not the level.
Take it, and it becomes your sound. Press Offer again, and that's a pass.
Once you've heard it, either answer teaches the model what you like.
Wander lets the model play the controls with you.
A little, and ideas grow into B.
Further, and the knobs drift toward your taste.
All the way up, and it roams.
Structure never changes on its own. A new module only arrives as an offer.
Touch anything, and it waits for you. Freeze holds it where it is.
Keep makes the sound you hear home.
Then go as far out as you like.
Back glides you home.
Keep also puts the sound on the workbench, so PATCH shows what you kept.
Hold latches the notes you play.
Unison stacks all four voices on one note.
Glide slides a line from note to note, and chords stay clean.
The arpeggiator plays a held chord up, down or both ways, at the tempo you set.
Sync puts the patch's own step sequencer on that tempo too.
And when you like what you're playing, REC keeps it as a WAV file.
Plug in a controller and turn its knobs. The first eight you turn claim the eight controls.
Learn moves any control to the next knob you touch.
Pressure pushes Bright, and the mod wheel drives Motion.
The sustain pedal holds what you let go of, and MIDI clock sets the tempo.
With two tabs open, MIDI plays the one you used last. The other stands aside, and says so.
Now all of it at once.
An arpeggio at eighty-four, Wander drifting, and an offer growing in B.
When it sounds right, take it on the downbeat.
That's PERFORM: play it, turn it, and let it offer.
Next, open the patch in PATCH, and see what the sound is made of.
